title: Herpes simplex: genital herpes and cold sores (adult)
subject: infectious-disease
setting: Outpatient, sexual health clinic, emergency department
summary: Treat first-episode genital herpes with oral aciclovir, valaciclovir or famciclovir (CDC 7 to 10 days; BASHH 5 days with review), use short episodic courses or daily suppression for recurrences, give suppression from 36 weeks of pregnancy, and treat cold sores early with high-dose valaciclovir.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Genital herpes: painful grouped vesicles and shallow ulcers on the genitals or perianal skin. A first episode may bring fever, myalgia, tender inguinal nodes, dysuria, urinary retention or aseptic meningitis. HSV-1 now causes many first genital episodes.
Recurrences: a prodrome of tingling or burning, then milder, shorter lesions. Genital HSV-2 recurs more often than genital HSV-1. Asymptomatic shedding is an important route of transmission.
Herpes proctitis in men who have sex with men: anorectal pain, discharge and tenesmus; consider empirical HSV treatment.
Cold sores (herpes labialis): prodrome then vesicles at the lip border; primary oral infection can present as gingivostomatitis.

Red flags: eye involvement (pain, photophobia, red eye, dendritic ulcer), eczema herpeticum, severe or disseminated disease in the immunocompromised, meningitis or encephalitis, and hepatitis in pregnancy.

sections.title: Investigations
items: Swab the base of a lesion for HSV PCR (NAAT) with typing; viral culture is less sensitive. Do not rely on a Tzanck smear.
Type-specific IgG serology only for selected questions (for example a partner with HSV, or late pregnancy). HSV IgM is not useful; low-index HSV-2 IgG results need confirmation.
Test for syphilis, HIV and other STIs in anyone with a genital ulcer.
First episode in late pregnancy: lesion PCR with typing plus type-specific serology helps distinguish a true primary infection from a first recognised recurrence.

sections.title: First episode genital herpes
items: Start an oral antiviral within 5 days of onset, or while new lesions are still forming or systemic symptoms persist.
CDC 2021: aciclovir 400 mg orally three times daily, or valaciclovir 1 g twice daily, or famciclovir 250 mg three times daily, for 7 to 10 days; extend if healing is incomplete.

BASHH 2024: aciclovir 400 mg three times daily or valaciclovir 500 mg twice daily for 5 days (alternatives aciclovir 200 mg five times daily or famciclovir 250 mg three times daily). Review at day 5 and continue if new lesions or complications; give 7 to 10 days if review is not possible.
Supportive care: saline bathing, analgesia, and 5% lidocaine ointment before passing urine. Topical antivirals add nothing to oral treatment.

Admit for urinary retention (consider a suprapubic catheter), meningism, severe systemic illness or inability to swallow. Severe disease: aciclovir 5 to 10 mg/kg IV 8-hourly, then oral to complete at least 10 days.

sections.title: Recurrent genital herpes
items: Agree a strategy with the patient: supportive care only, episodic treatment, or daily suppression; it can change over time.

Episodic (start at the prodrome or within 1 day of lesions; patient-held supply): aciclovir 800 mg three times daily for 2 days, or valaciclovir 500 mg twice daily for 3 days, or famciclovir 1 g twice daily for 1 day.

Suppression for frequent or distressing recurrences or to cut transmission: aciclovir 400 mg twice daily, or valaciclovir 500 mg once daily (1 g once daily if 10 or more recurrences a year), or famciclovir 250 mg twice daily. It reduces recurrences by 70% to 80%.
Breakthrough on suppression: aciclovir 400 mg three times daily or valaciclovir 500 mg twice daily (BASHH). Do not use once-daily aciclovir.
Stop suppression after up to 1 year to reassess, observing at least 2 recurrences before restarting. People taking it to reduce transmission should not take breaks.
Counsel on asymptomatic shedding, condoms, avoiding sex during lesions and prodrome, and disclosure; valaciclovir 500 mg daily reduces transmission to an uninfected partner.

sections.title: Cold sores (herpes labialis)
items: Most episodes settle without treatment. Advise avoiding kissing and oral sex while lesions are present, and sunscreen if sunlight triggers recurrences.
Topical aciclovir 5% cream applied 5 times daily from the prodrome gives only modest benefit.
Valaciclovir 2 g orally every 12 hours for 1 day (2 doses), started at the earliest symptom (FDA label).

Valaciclovir renal adjustment for cold sores: creatinine clearance 30 to 49 mL/min 1 g every 12 hours for 2 doses; 10 to 29 mL/min 500 mg every 12 hours for 2 doses; below 10 mL/min 500 mg single dose.
Refer urgently for eye involvement, eczema herpeticum, or extensive lesions in an immunocompromised patient.

sections.title: Pregnancy
items: First episode in pregnancy: oral aciclovir at usual doses (IV if severe) and early obstetric referral. Neonatal transmission risk is 30% to 50% when herpes is acquired near delivery, and below 1% with recurrent herpes or infection acquired in the first half of pregnancy.
Suppression from 36 weeks for women with genital herpes: aciclovir 400 mg three times daily or valaciclovir 500 mg twice daily until delivery; it reduces caesarean delivery.
Caesarean delivery is recommended when genital herpetic lesions are present at the onset of labour.
First episode in the third trimester, particularly within 6 weeks of delivery: caesarean is usually advised; manage with obstetrics under the joint BASHH/RCOG pregnancy guideline.
Tell the neonatal team about any maternal HSV near delivery. Neonatal herpes: aciclovir 20 mg/kg IV 8-hourly for 14 days (skin, eye, mouth) or 21 days (CNS or disseminated).

sections.title: HIV, immunosuppression and complications
items: HIV, episodic: aciclovir 400 mg three times daily or valaciclovir 1 g twice daily for 5 to 10 days (CDC).
HIV, suppression: aciclovir 400 to 800 mg two to three times daily, or valaciclovir 500 mg twice daily, or famciclovir 500 mg twice daily.

Lesions not healing on treatment in an immunocompromised patient: suspect aciclovir resistance, send swab for culture and resistance testing, and seek specialist advice. Foscarnet 80 to 120 mg/kg/day IV in 2 to 3 divided doses is the usual option (CDC).
Suspected HSV encephalitis: aciclovir 10 mg/kg IV 8-hourly immediately (see Acute encephalitis syndrome protocol).
Reduce aciclovir, valaciclovir and famciclovir doses in renal impairment, and keep patients well hydrated on IV aciclovir (crystal nephropathy).

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Starting episodic treatment late: benefit is greatest when taken at the prodrome.
Using topical antivirals for genital herpes.
Diagnosing an ulcer by serology or IgM instead of a lesion PCR, and missing syphilis.
Missing herpetic eye disease in a patient with facial cold sores.
Full-dose valaciclovir in older people or CKD without renal adjustment (confusion, neurotoxicity).

drugs.name: Aciclovir (acyclovir), oral
drugs.dose: First episode 400 mg three times daily for 5 to 10 days; episodic 800 mg three times daily for 2 days; suppression 400 mg twice daily; pregnancy from 36 weeks 400 mg three times daily

drugs.name: Valaciclovir (valacyclovir)
drugs.dose: First episode 1 g twice daily (CDC) or 500 mg twice daily (BASHH); episodic 500 mg twice daily for 3 days; suppression 500 mg once daily (1 g if 10 or more recurrences a year); cold sores 2 g every 12 hours for 1 day
drugs.notes: Renal adjustment needed; pregnancy suppression 500 mg twice daily from 36 weeks.

drugs.name: Famciclovir
drugs.dose: First episode 250 mg three times daily; episodic 1 g twice daily for 1 day; suppression 250 mg twice daily (500 mg twice daily in HIV)

drugs.name: Aciclovir, IV
drugs.dose: 5 to 10 mg/kg IV 8-hourly for severe genital or disseminated disease; 10 mg/kg 8-hourly for encephalitis
drugs.notes: Hydrate; adjust for renal function. Neonates 20 mg/kg 8-hourly.

drugs.name: Foscarnet
drugs.dose: 80 to 120 mg/kg/day IV in 2 to 3 divided doses
drugs.notes: Aciclovir-resistant HSV; specialist use; nephrotoxic, causes electrolyte disturbance.

drugs.name: Lidocaine 5% ointment
drugs.dose: Apply thinly to lesions as needed, especially before passing urine
